examples.en: For my health, I'm quitting smoking from this year.
My father quit smoking after visiting the hospital.
I will definitely quit smoking next year.

examples.ko: 금연하는 사람이 요즘 많이 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: More people are quitting smoking these days.

examples.ko: 한 달 동안 금연하고 운동도 시작했어요.
examples.en: I quit smoking for a month and started exercising too.
My cough got better because I quit smoking.

explain: 스스로 담배를 끊을 때 '금연하다'를 쓰고, 말할 때는 '담배를 끊다'도 많이 써요. 장소의 규칙은 '금연 구역'처럼 명사로 말하고, 반대말은 '흡연하다'예요.

phrases.en: I quit smoking last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 '금연하다' 대신 많이 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common spoken alternative to 금연하다.

phrases.en: I'm quitting smoking right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 담배를 참고 있는 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you are currently in the middle of quitting.
phrases.en_equiv: to be in the middle of quitting smoking

phrases.en: This is a no-smoking area.
phrases.nuance_ko: 담배를 피울 수 없는 장소를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a place where smoking is not allowed.

explain_en: Use 금연하다 when you yourself give up smoking; in speech 담배를 끊다 is also very common. A place's rule is said as a noun, like 금연 구역, and the opposite verb is 흡연하다.

examples.en: I disinfect wounds with medicine.
Yesterday I disinfected the room thoroughly.
They will disinfect the school classrooms tomorrow.
They are disinfecting, so the smell is a bit strong.
Disinfect your hands and go inside.

examples.ko: 컵을 끓는 물에 소독해서 다시 썼어요.
examples.en: I sterilized the cup in boiling water and used it again.

explain: '청소하다'는 더러운 것을 치우는 일이고 '소독하다'는 균을 없애는 일이라서 같이 하는 경우가 많아요. '소독약', '손 소독제'처럼 다른 말과 붙여 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I disinfected the knee I hurt when I fell.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다친 곳에 약을 발라 균을 없앨 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when cleaning an injury to kill germs.

phrases.en: There is disinfectant in the drawer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소독할 때 쓰는 약을 말하는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for the medicine used to disinfect.

phrases.en: There is hand sanitizer in front of the shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손에 바르는 소독 제품을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A product you put on your hands to disinfect.

explain_en: '청소하다' is clearing away dirt and '소독하다' is killing germs, so people often do both together. It combines with other words, as in '소독약' and '손 소독제'.

examples.en: A gentle aroma spread through the room.

examples.ko: 자기 전에 아로마를 맡으면 마음이 편해져요.
examples.en: Smelling an aroma before bed calms my mind.

examples.ko: 아로마는 향이 강해서 조금만 써야 해요.
examples.en: Aromas are strong, so you should use only a little.
This shop also sells aroma candles.
I relaxed my body with aromatherapy at the massage shop.

examples.ko: 아로마도 좋지만 환기도 꼭 해 주세요.
examples.en: Aroma is nice, but please be sure to ventilate too.

explain: '아로마 오일', '아로마 양초'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙어서 식물에서 얻은 향과 관련된 것을 말해요. 일상의 좋은 냄새는 '향기'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I dropped a few drops of aroma oil.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식물에서 얻은 향이 나는 기름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An oil with a scent taken from plants.

phrases.en: I lit an aroma candle and relaxed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋은 향이 나는 양초예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A candle that gives off a pleasant scent.

phrases.en: There is an aroma scent in the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아로마 제품에서 나는 향을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The scent that comes from aroma products.

explain_en: It usually sits in front of another word, as in 아로마 오일 or 아로마 양초, for things related to plant-derived scent. An ordinary pleasant smell is called 향기.

examples.en: I got a silver bracelet as a birthday gift.
The bracelet fits my wrist just right.
A name is engraved on the bracelet.

examples.ko: 팔찌는 손목에 차고 반지는 손가락에 껴요.
examples.en: You wear a bracelet on the wrist and a ring on the finger.
I want to buy a bracelet too.
I bought a bracelet and necklace as a set.

explain: 팔찌는 '차다'나 '하다'와 같이 써서 '팔찌를 차다'라고 말해요. 반지는 '끼다'를 써서 동사가 달라요.

phrases.en: I wear a bracelet every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팔찌에는 '차다'를 써요. 반지는 '끼다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 차다 with bracelets. For rings, use 끼다.

phrases.en: I came out wearing a bracelet today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '차다'보다 가볍게, 꾸민다는 느낌으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A lighter way to say it, with a sense of accessorizing.

phrases.en: My grandmother gave me a gold bracelet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재료 이름을 앞에 붙여 팔찌 종류를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the material before the word to say what kind of bracelet it is.

explain_en: A bracelet goes with 'chada' or 'hada': 'paljjireul chada'. A ring uses 'kkida', so the verb is different.

en: to rest; to take a break

examples.en: On weekends I rest at home.
I took a short break after work.
The doctor told me to rest for a week.
If you are tired, take a short rest and come back.
I listened to music while I rested.

examples.ko: 내일은 아무것도 안 하고 휴식할 거예요.
examples.en: Tomorrow I will do nothing and just rest.

explain: 대화에서는 보통 '쉬다'를 써요. '휴식하다'는 안내문이나 글에서 더 딱딱하게 들려요. 명사 '휴식'은 '휴식을 취하다', '휴식 시간'처럼 말할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: I'm tired, so I rest well at home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대화에서는 '휴식하다'보다 '쉬다'를 훨씬 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In conversation, people use 쉬다 much more often than 휴식하다.

phrases.en: I took a short rest during lunch break.
phrases.nuance_ko: '휴식하다'와 뜻은 같고, 명사 '휴식'에 '을 취하다'를 붙여 조금 더 격식 있게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but built on the noun 휴식 and sounds a bit more formal.

phrases.en: I drink coffee during the break.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쉬는 시간을 가리키는 말로, 안내문이나 일정표에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to break time; common on notices and schedules.

explain_en: In everyday speech people usually say '쉬다'. '휴식하다' sounds stiffer and fits notices and writing. The noun works in speech too: '휴식을 취하다' (take a rest) and '휴식 시간' (break time).

t90.ax: On weekends I rest at home.

examples.en: Is there a health food store near here?

examples.ko: 건강식품을 사라고 강권하는 바람에 모임에 나가기가 싫어졌어요.
examples.en: They kept pushing me to buy health supplements, so I stopped wanting to go to the meetings.
I picked out health food to give to my parents.
Everyday eating habits matter more than health food.

examples.ko: 이 건강식품은 하루에 한 알만 먹어요.
examples.en: You take just one tablet of this health supplement a day.

examples.ko: 건강식품을 살 때는 성분을 꼭 확인하세요.
examples.en: When buying health food, be sure to check the ingredients.

explain: 비타민, 홍삼처럼 건강을 위해 먹는 식품을 말해요. '건강기능식품'이라고도 해요. 명절이나 어버이날에 부모님께 선물로 드리기도 해요.

phrases.en: I bought health supplements as a gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: '건강식품'과 같은 뜻으로, 가게나 포장에 이렇게 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 건강식품, common on shops and packaging.

phrases.en: I take health food regularly every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: '챙겨 먹다'는 잊지 않고 꾸준히 먹는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 챙겨 먹다 means to take it regularly without forgetting.

phrases.en: I gave health food to my parents as a gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어버이날이나 명절 선물로 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears as a gift for holidays like Parents' Day.

explain_en: It refers to food taken for health, such as vitamins and red ginseng. It is also called '건강기능식품'. People sometimes give it to their parents as a gift at holidays or Parents' Day.

examples.en: On rainy days, I think of sujebi.
You tear off thin pieces of dough and put them in.

examples.ko: 어머니가 끓여 주신 수제비가 제일 맛있어요.
examples.en: The sujebi my mother made is the most delicious.
For lunch, I ate sujebi instead of kalguksu.

examples.ko: 수제비에 감자랑 애호박을 넣으면 더 맛있어요.
examples.en: It tastes better if you add potato and zucchini to the sujebi.
Please give me one more bowl of sujebi.

explain: 칼국수와 비슷해 보이지만, 수제비는 반죽을 칼로 썰지 않고 손으로 떼어 넣어요. 그래서 모양이 조금씩 달라요.

phrases.example: 엄마가 비 오는 날 수제비를 끓여 주셨어요.
phrases.en: My mom made sujebi for me on a rainy day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수제비를 만들어 요리한다는 뜻으로 가장 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to say you cook sujebi.

phrases.en: I had potato sujebi for lunch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감자를 넣은 수제비예요. 재료 이름을 앞에 붙여 종류를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sujebi with potato; you put the ingredient before the word to name the type.

phrases.en: One bowl of sujebi, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당에서 주문할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when ordering at a restaurant.

explain_en: It looks similar to kalguksu, but sujebi dough is torn by hand instead of cut with a knife. That is why each piece has a slightly different shape.

examples.en: I bought rice flour to make rice cakes.
Bread made from rice flour is very chewy.
If you mix rice flour into the batter, it gets crispier.

examples.ko: 쌀가루 반죽을 한 시간 동안 두세요.
examples.en: Leave the rice flour dough for an hour.
Can I use rice flour instead of wheat flour?
Store the rice flour in a cool place.

explain: 짝이 되는 말은 '밀가루'예요. 떡, 전, 빵을 만들 때 쌀가루를 쓰기도 하는데, 밀가루와 반죽 느낌이 달라서 레시피대로 쓰는 게 좋아요.

phrases.en: Rice flour dough sticks to your hands easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쌀가루로 만든 반죽을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to dough made from rice flour.

phrases.en: Add water to one cup of rice flour.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리법에서 양을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for amounts in a recipe.

phrases.en: I use rice flour instead of wheat flour.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밀가루 대신 쓴다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you substitute it for wheat flour.
phrases.en_equiv: rice flour instead of wheat flour

explain_en: Its counterpart is '밀가루' (wheat flour). Rice flour is also used for rice cakes, pancakes and bread, but the dough feels different from wheat dough, so it is best to follow the recipe.

examples.en: I sliced the squash thinly and put it in the soybean paste stew.
My mother made squash pancakes for me.

examples.ko: 애호박이 싱싱해서 마트에서 두 개 샀어요.
examples.en: The squash was fresh, so I bought two at the supermarket.
I stir-fried the squash and ate it as a side dish.
Young squash is softer and more tender than old pumpkin.
One squash is enough to make soup.

explain: 덜 자란 어린 호박이라서 껍질이 얇고 부드러워요. 다 익어 단단해진 '늙은호박'과 구별해요. 주키니와 비슷하게 쓰이지만 한국 요리에서는 전, 찌개, 볶음에 자주 넣어요.

phrases.en: We made a lot of zucchini pancakes for Chuseok.
phrases.nuance_ko: 애호박을 얇게 썰어 부친 전이에요. 명절에 자주 먹어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Thinly sliced zucchini fried in batter, often eaten at holidays.

phrases.en: For dinner I made stir-fried zucchini as a side dish.
phrases.nuance_ko: 애호박을 볶은 간단한 반찬이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simple stir-fried side dish made with zucchini.

phrases.en: I cut the zucchini into half-moon shapes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리를 준비할 때 쓰는 동작이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A cooking-prep action.

explain_en: It is an immature, young pumpkin, so the skin is thin and soft. It is distinguished from the fully ripened, hard '늙은호박'. It is used similarly to zucchini, and in Korean cooking it often goes into pancakes, stews and stir-fries.

examples.en: I lightly applied powder to my face.
This powder smells nice.
I ran out of powder, so I need to buy more.
I prevented heat rash with baby powder.
I always use powder when I put on makeup.
I took a powder puff out in the restroom.

explain: 화장품에서는 얼굴에 바르는 가루를 말해요. 음식 재료는 '가루'라고 하지만, '단백질 파우더'처럼 외래어 이름에는 '파우더'를 그대로 써요.

phrases.en: I put on powder after washing my face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화장할 때 얼굴에 바르는 가루에 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The usual pairing for makeup powder applied to the face.

phrases.en: I have protein powder after working out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹는 가루 제품 이름에도 '파우더'를 그대로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word is also kept as-is in names of edible powder products.

phrases.en: I mix this powder in water and drink it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '파우더'와 같은 뜻의 우리말이에요. 음식 재료에 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: A native Korean word with the same meaning, more natural for food ingredients.

explain_en: In cosmetics it means the loose powder you put on your face. Food ingredients are usually called 가루, but loanword names like 단백질 파우더 keep 파우더.

examples.en: If you pass the national exam, you get a license.
To become a nurse, you have to take a national exam.
I practically live in the library preparing for the national exam.
On the day of the national exam, I was nervous from the morning.
When the national exam is over, I'm going on a trip.
The national exam results come out next week.

explain: 의사, 간호사, 변호사처럼 나라에서 자격을 주는 시험을 말해요. 보통 '국가시험을 보다/치르다', '국가시험에 합격하다'로 써요.

phrases.en: I'm preparing for next year's state exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험 공부를 하는 중일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you are studying for the exam.
phrases.en_equiv: to prepare for the state exam

phrases.en: I passed the state exam, so I'm really happy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험 결과가 좋을 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the exam result is good.

phrases.en: I failed the state exam, so I'm studying again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 합격하지 못했을 때 쓰는 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An everyday way to say you did not pass.

explain_en: It refers to exams that grant a state-recognized qualification, as for doctors, nurses or lawyers. It is typically used as '국가시험을 보다/치르다' or '국가시험에 합격하다'.

examples.en: Let's wrap up today's work here.
I closed the presentation with a greeting.
I'll finish the report by tomorrow.
I want to end it on a good note.
What's a good way to wrap up this year?
I rushed to finish and made a mistake.

explain: '마무리하다'는 일의 끝 부분을 잘 정리해 끝낼 때 써요. 그냥 '끝내다'보다 마지막 손질을 한다는 느낌이 있어요. '일을 마무리하다', '마무리 짓다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: Let's wrap up today's meeting here.
phrases.nuance_ko: '마무리하다'와 뜻이 같고, 끝을 낸다는 느낌이 조금 더 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, with a slightly stronger sense of bringing it to an end.

phrases.en: The construction will be finished next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 저절로 끝나는 쪽을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the work comes to an end by itself.

phrases.en: I'll finish my work and go home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일을 끝낸 다음 다른 일을 이어 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Links finishing something to the next action.

explain_en: 마무리하다 means tidying up and ending the last part of a task well. Compared with plain 끝내다, it gives the feel of putting on finishing touches. You say '일을 마무리하다' or '마무리 짓다'.

dis.h: wrap up a task with final touches
gh: formal: someone ends or shuts something
formal: concludes a case or war

p.n: 종료하다 formally declares an end; 마무리하다 means wrapping up and finishing off.

t90.ax: Let's wrap up today's work here.

examples.ko: 머리가 아파서 양호실에 가서 누워 있었어요.
examples.en: My head hurt, so I went to the nurse's office and lay down.
The nurse's office teacher got medicine for me.
I fell during gym class and went to the nurse's office.

examples.ko: 양호실에는 침대 두 개가 놓여 있어요.
examples.en: There are two beds in the nurse's office.

examples.ko: 열이 나면 먼저 양호실에 가 보세요.
examples.en: If you have a fever, go to the nurse's office first.
After resting a little in the nurse's office, I felt better.

explain: 학교에서 아픈 학생을 돌보는 방이에요. 요즘 학교에서는 '보건실'이라고 많이 불러요. 같은 장소를 가리키는 말이라서 어른들은 옛날 말인 '양호실'을 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: My stomach hurt, so I went to the nurse's office.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요즘 학교에서 더 많이 쓰는 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name more commonly used in schools these days.

phrases.en: I had a fever, so I rested in the infirmary.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아플 때 잠깐 누워 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when lying down for a while because you feel sick.

phrases.en: The school nurse put a bandage on me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 양호실에서 학생을 돌봐 주는 선생님을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The way to refer to the teacher who looks after students in the infirmary.

explain_en: It is the room at school where sick students are looked after. Schools today often call it '보건실'. It refers to the same place, and adults sometimes still use the older word '양호실'.

examples.ko: 이 에세이는 여행 이야기를 담고 있어요.
examples.en: This essay is full of travel stories.
I write a short essay every weekend.

examples.ko: 친구가 추천한 에세이 책을 읽고 있어요.
examples.en: I am reading an essay book my friend recommended.

examples.ko: 그 작가는 소설보다 에세이로 더 유명해요.
examples.en: That author is better known for essays than for novels.
You can feel the author's honest thoughts in the essay.
The newly released essay collection is popular at bookstores.

explain: 소설과 달리 지은이의 경험과 생각을 쓴 글을 가리켜요. 서점에서는 '소설', '시', '에세이'처럼 갈래 이름으로도 봐요. 같은 뜻의 한자어로 '수필'도 있어요.

phrases.en: That author wrote many essays.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에세이'와 같은 뜻의 한자어예요. 책이나 글을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A Sino-Korean word meaning the same as '에세이', common for books and writing.

phrases.en: I read essays before going to bed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글을 읽을 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for reading this kind of writing.

phrases.example: 제 꿈은 에세이 작가가 되는 거예요.
phrases.en: My dream is to become an essay writer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 에세이를 쓰는 사람을 말할 때 '작가'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '작가' to refer to a person who writes essays.

explain_en: Unlike a novel, it is writing based on the author's own experiences and thoughts. Bookstores use it as a genre label next to novels and poems. A Sino-Korean word with the same sense, 수필, also exists.

t90.ax: I write a short essay every weekend.
